title: Cooldown-preserving flat veto route-substitution test
thesis: When a frozen flat-regime stale-inventory veto rejects an otherwise valid signal, reserving the same seven-day cooldown timestamp will prevent unintended substitution into non-flat DRA inventory and improve matched-capital inventory risk without sacrificing total PnL.
mechanism: The quality veto currently changes the shared reservation calendar; preserving the rejected signal's cooldown isolates signal quality from route timing and removes replacement entries caused only by the veto.
economic_rationale: The predecessor changed the intended stale-inventory mechanism but failed because route substitution added non-flat inventory. Holding the reservation calendar fixed tests the causal source of that opportunity cost without scanning thresholds.
